title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #207
gist: This week's Not Boring digest covers five developments: Merck/Moderna's mRNA melanoma vaccine hit its first successful Phase III readout as an adjuvant to Keytruda; a Nature Human Behavior study showed voluntary attention regulates immune response; robotics startup Generalist's GEN-1.5 demonstrated one-shot learning; Stripe's reported $7.5B acquisition of OpenRouter kicked off a wave of competing 'router' launches from Ramp and Not Boring portfolio company Merge; and Uber, Amazon and DoorDash all expanded drone-delivery programs in the same week, prompting Packy McCormick to declare himself 'incredibly bullish on flight.'

insights.claim: Merck and Moderna's personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, given alongside Keytruda after surgery in high-risk melanoma patients, significantly reduced the risk of cancer recurrence or spread compared with Keytruda alone in a Phase III trial — the first successful late-stage trial for a personalized mRNA cancer therapy, with potential approval and launch around 2027.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: First successful Phase III readout for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine — a proof point for the mRNA-oncology combination-therapy thesis with a plausible 2027 approval/launch timeline to track.
insights.locator: (1) Merck-Moderna mRNA Cancer Vaccine Successful in Phase III

insights.claim: Even after this Phase III success, the personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine remains expensive and complicated, and the result covers only one cancer type so far.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Tempers the immediate commercial read-through: cost and complexity are stated hurdles even after trial success, meaning near-term revenue impact is likely gradual rather than an immediate margin driver.
insights.quote: the vaccine is still expensive and complicated
insights.locator: Melanoma is just one kind of cancer

insights.claim: A Nature Human Behavior study (Mizrachi, Rottem and Rozenkrantz) established that voluntarily directed attention can regulate acute immune responses in humans, reframing perception as biologically consequential rather than merely experiential.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An early but notable data point in mind-body/psychoneuroimmunology research, with plausible future intersection with digital-therapeutics and biofeedback product theses.
insights.quote: These results establish attention as a cognitive mechanism capable of regulating immune function in vivo.
insights.locator: (2) Voluntary attention regulates acute immune responses in humans

insights.claim: Robotics company Generalist's GEN-1.5 is a one-shot learner: shown a few seconds of demonstration data, it can figure out a task, learning from simulation, from watching humans, or by chaining together smaller tasks.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A capability datapoint for the generalist-robot investment thesis — one-shot imitation learning is a key bottleneck that needs to fall before general-purpose robots scale; worth tracking Generalist as a company.

insights.claim: Stripe is acquiring OpenRouter, the leading AI model-routing provider founded by OpenSea founder Alex Atallah, for a reported $7.5 billion per the New York Times; in the same week, Not Boring portfolio companies Merge (with Merge for Workforce, cutting token spend 75x) and Ramp (which bought the domain router.com for its own Router product) both launched competing router offerings.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: AI model-routing is consolidating fast into a distinct infrastructure layer — the Stripe/OpenRouter deal size ($7.5B) is a real valuation marker for the category, and Merge/Ramp's simultaneous launches signal routing is becoming table stakes for AI-adjacent fintech and workflow platforms.

insights.claim: 'Return on Tokens' (ROT), a metric flagged earlier by Markie Wagner, is becoming the efficiency benchmark companies optimize for, with routers as the mechanism to get the right AI model at the lowest price automatically.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: 'Return on Tokens' is a candidate KPI to watch for in AI-native software vendors' investor materials — a sign the market is shifting from raw model-capability comparisons to cost-efficiency-per-token as the competitive axis.
insights.locator: In early June, Markie Wagner told us

insights.claim: Zipline and Uber announced a partnership under which Uber will invest in the drone company to scale deliveries; separately, Amazon is reportedly expanding Prime Air to 500 cities by year-end, and DoorDash launched its own DoorDash Air drone program — all in the same week.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Multiple large logistics players (Uber, Amazon, DoorDash) simultaneously scaling drone delivery in the same week is a concrete signal that last-mile drone delivery is moving from pilot to scaled rollout — relevant for logistics, drone-hardware and airspace-regulation-exposed names.

insights.claim: Packy McCormick states he is 'incredibly bullish on flight' based on this cluster of drone-delivery news, viewing it as just the beginning.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A stated high-conviction bullish call on 'flight' (drones/aerial logistics) as an investable theme, worth tracking against Not Boring Capital's portfolio positioning.
insights.quote: I am incredibly bullish on flight and think these bits of news are just the beginning.
insights.locator: I am incredibly bullish on flight
